text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel under heavy political fire after witnesses say he called Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer a "real pig" during the EU summit in Amsterdam. Schuessel denies ever uttering the words.
- Creditanstalt has sold its leasing subsidiary AVA-Bank for over one billion schillings to GE Capital.
- A study by a German expert for Austria's pension system says that the retirement age should be the same for women and men after the year 2005.
- Germany's Ifo institute says Austria will not meet the EMU convergence criterium of a total debt of 60 percent of gross domestic product.
- Price commission gives the go-ahead for the Post's new cost structure in the telecoms industry which is expected to lead to a strong increase in the cost of local calls.
- UIAG plans to make electronic goods retailer Niedermeyer fit for flotation.
- The government and the civil servants union, at loggerheads over the former's savings drive in the public sector, will meet today to hammer out a schedule for their next negotiations.

- A decision on the future of the investment banks of Creditanstalt and Bank Austria, now still running as separate institutions, will be decided on Wednesday. The two are expected to be merged into one.
- Interior Minister Karl Schloegl says Austria will open its borders with Germany and Italy step by step.
- VA Tech Industrieanlagenbau (VAI) has lost out to ECF-Kaiser of the U.S. for an order to build a steelworks in the Czech Republic at Nova Hut. VAI had been negotiating the deal for three years.

- States in the east of Austria will show a significantly stronger rate of economic growth up to 2001 than those in the west, a study by the European Economic Research and Advisory Consortium said. Strongest growth is seen in Lower Austria and Burgenland with an annual 2.7 and 2.1 percent respectively.
